title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Seven fixes that had fixed too much
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.34 undoes seven side effects of its own recent fixes. The dead code detector had gone silent on whole projects, renaming a folder killed the initial index, a `gradlew clean` froze the window, and the Screen Flow map took seconds to open on a large workspace.

highlights.title: Dead code detection is back
highlights.description: A root build file declaring `alias(libs.plugins.maven.publish) apply false` made the whole workspace read as published API, so nothing was ever reported.

highlights.title: Renaming a folder keeps the index
highlights.description: Adding or renaming a folder cancelled every scan in flight, the initial index included.

highlights.title: No more freeze on build or map
highlights.description: A `gradlew clean` no longer sweeps the index per deleted file, and the Screen Flow map skips files that hold no navigation.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A plugin declared with `apply false` no longer marks its module, or the project root, as published.
A folder added or renamed is indexed on its own scan instead of cancelling the one in progress.
The delete watcher honours the exclude patterns, so build output no longer triggers a full index sweep.
The Screen Flow map skips files without a route or a navigation before scanning their comments.
The Logcat error banner survives the rows already in flight, `items.all { }` no longer silences the Remote Config detector, and a capped listing blocks permission removal too.
